notes: Company background: mid-stage SaaS that provides embedded help center + in-app support; heavy KB (user guides, logs, KB articles) - currently using keyword search with Elastic, moving to semantic RAG for higher recall.
Indexing scale: current ~3M documents (help articles, transcripts, logs). Growth plan: expected to reach 10-15M docs in 12-18 months. Wants clear guidance on index sharding and vector store sizing.
QPS profile: high query traffic during business hours; avg steady-state 400-700 QPS, burst to 2k QPS for peak support events. Require predictable P95 latency under 120ms for reranked responses.
Cost sensitivity: unit economics target is <$0.003 per query (embeddings + rerank amortized). Wants tradeoff options: cheaper embed model + smaller reranker for non-critical flows.
Model preference: open-embedding model recommended by infra team but CTO wants Redwood to provide vetted performance profiles and fallback to smaller models when cost constrained.

Reranking approach: prefer lightweight reranker (cross-encoder) for top-10 candidates; explore hybrid (BM25 + dense) for initial recall. Need Redwood to show batching + caching benefits on hosted API.
Latency controls requested: continuous batching windows, prefix/KV cache for chat contexts, region-aware routing, and automatic fallback to cached results under load.
Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SSO via SAML, audit log retention 12 months, EU residency for EU customers' documents. KMS integration required for key management.
Quote from CTO (paraphrase): 'We cannot let reranking push p95 above 120ms — users will notice. Also need a predictable per-query cost model for forecasting.'
Operational asks: token-level cost breakdown per route, per-model latency histogram, and an eval harness for regression detection tied to prompt sets.

POC scope: ingest 1M docs, build embeddings, run 500 QPS sustained with occasional 2k QPS bursts; compare three rerank model options (high-accuracy, mid, low-cost) and report cost/latency/quality tradeoffs.
SE notes: recommend Redwood Optimize suggestions: quantization candidate list, batching/window tuning, and prefix caching on high-frequency user queries.
Legal/Procurement: procurement timeline ~6-8 weeks after successful POC. Wants simple commit options for 12-month reserved capacity if SLA meets targets.
Internal ops concern: can hosted API support sustained high-QPS with per-customer burst without dedicated capacity? SE to confirm autoscaling and burst policy details.
